subject: Computer Networking
title: VLANs and Trunking
description: A 60-second lesson on VLANs and Trunking.

hook.text: One physical switch, three separate networks. VLANs do that without extra hardware.

buildup.text: A VLAN logically groups switch ports. Devices in different VLANs can't see each other at Layer 2.

discovery.text: VLAN tagging adds a small header to each frame identifying its VLAN. The tag is a 12-bit ID.

twist.text: Trunk ports carry multiple VLANs between switches. Without trunks, each VLAN needs its own cable.

climax.text: VLANs boost security: accounting can't sniff engineering's traffic, even on the same switch.

punchline.text: VLANs split one switch into many virtual networks. Smart and cheap.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of using VLANs?
options: Logically separating networks on the same physical switch
Increasing the speed of all network connections

details.summary: VLANs logically segment a physical switch into separate broadcast domains, isolating traffic between groups of devices without separate physical infrastructure. Trunk links carry traffic from multiple VLANs between switches using 802.1Q tags that identify which VLAN each frame belongs to.
details.whyItMatters: VLANs are the primary tool for network segmentation in every enterprise. They improve security, reduce broadcast traffic, and organize the network logically regardless of physical location.
takeaways: VLANs create isolated broadcast domains on shared switches
802.1Q trunk ports carry multiple VLANs between switches
VLAN segmentation improves both security and performance

faq.question: How do VLANs improve security?
faq.answer: VLANs isolate traffic so devices in one VLAN cannot see or access devices in another without going through a router or Layer 3 switch with access controls. This keeps sensitive traffic like finance or management separate from general office traffic on the same physical switches.

faq.question: What is a trunk port?
faq.answer: A trunk port carries traffic from multiple VLANs on a single link by adding an 802.1Q tag to each frame identifying its VLAN. Switch-to-switch connections and switch-to-router connections use trunk ports. Access ports carry traffic for a single VLAN and are used for end devices.
